vacuous_or_weak: RestartLimitGhost: says R8; can fail (D7-RESTART F 17 under a mutation); gf is the model's own count at the fence site, independent of rs
StaleWrites: stronger than R6's text (also forbids a session start), matches R57; can fail
CommitRecordStable: says R14; fails only with both WX and the epoch check removed; WX still not shown load-bearing with the epoch check
SlotsProc/SlotsR10: say R10 and amended R10; their only failure is not as built, and D7_SLOTS was never run with the as-built close (under D7_SLOTS alone the commit closes the child, an oracle)
LoopReported: says R5; fails under the mutation, BOUNDED with the rule

WakeSourceAlive: a reading of R6's bound with the amended clause; counts a child as a source (weaker than R6); on a first turn one fault silences, so R6's 'both' needs restating or the bound is broken - an owner wording question
WakeChainBounded and AlarmsBounded: proxies with no rule text behind them; WakeChainBounded cannot tell D1's never-quiescing loop from three turns of one outage
fault_accounting: One fault each: x turn death (or a crash killing background commands, same price), u an outage of any length, y alarm.json unreadable until re-registration, o a whole turn's acts omitted, p one pause, l one lost wake, z one unconfirmed stop, t one torn commit, r one reset (a left run.lock free), child faults. Free: transcript lag, READY in flight, a stale coordinator breaking R6, duplicate starts, commit before bind, early or mid-turn alarm exits, superseded exits, list recovery, slow/stuck return, owner acts. Untimed: millisecond and hour windows are equally free, the source of every timing-dependent verdict. One u buys the whole D1 chain.
fairness: Weak fairness per process id over fault-free edges; owner wake only after two losses (l+x) or a reset, but owner zombie end and fresh-coordinator start always fair; environment ids 30/31 never forced; planned choices allowed in cycles; coordinator plan alternatives not forced. Liveness 'holds' rests on the owner and on the stop/close merges; no liveness verdict exists for AB-ALL.
r57: Partly met. The eight named mechanisms (M1-M6, RC, CE) are modelled from what is on disk, each with a counterexample that walks against the scripts. Not met as a whole: stop/close still partly oracle (z -> stopped, no ticks), timeliness for all but one slow call, the stale coordinator reads the live table, host class from a reset flag, and no complete configuration with every flag on (AB-ALL BOUNDED at 2,858,368 states, liveness unchecked; AB-WAKE-ALL keeps the fence group's oracles).

FX-CLAIM.verdict: relied on with a stated limit: safety only, under a stronger assumption than stated
limits: With FX_CLAIM on, MF:1144 lets a session only die before its first tool call; it cannot stall. The ablation trace uses exactly that stall (FX-CLAIM-X step 2), so the flag removes the fix and a behaviour. Reading (i) as modelled means every live session makes its first tool call, or dies, within the lease. INFERRED: allowing the stall fails Slots as in the ablation

Step 7 is modelled on true liveness (MF:240). The design counts dead folder sessions that have no done file, and nothing closes them in a tombstoned attempt. INFERRED liveness hole (slot leak); Slots carries over, liveness does not
No D7_SLOTS (SlotsProc and SlotsR10 unchecked), no AB_PROCLIST, no watcher death (H2); schedule 8 reaches only the uncharged part
